analysis:
The only change is a new pure helper, ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild(pinned:current:), added in ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift at head lines 448-456. It returns true only if every pinned member reported a digest and all digests are identical. It has no I/O, no key or crypto handling, no network and no authorization decisions. Within the supplied units it is not called, so any caller, such as the control leader's auto re-plan after an update, was not reviewed.

The helper fails closed. An empty pinned set, a missing digest or a nil digest returns false, which only delays a re-plan. The helper does not compare the digests to the pinned values. It checks only that the members agree with each other, so a caller that treated it as a trust check against the pinned digests would be wrong. Its documented purpose is readiness for re-planning, not authorization.

The retry path stays bounded by the existing retryAfterFailureSeconds and checkEverySeconds, and the helper adds no new availability exposure. The change touches no threat-model assets (A-001 to A-019) and no listed boundaries for this file. TB-013 and T-061 cover installer and add-on tampering, not the cluster update logic.

Open question for integration: whether the caller, outside the supplied evidence, still verifies the actual worker digests against a trusted source before re-adopting. If it treats oneBuild as sufficient, a compromised member's digest could be accepted once both members agree. That is not visible here and is not claimed as a finding.

The unit 835f62aa717dc58f:3 base text is the unchanged portion of the same file, and no regression was identified there.
